name: meeple-loop-cap-two-v1
description: THE CAP SWEEP, and the only one of the three meeple-loop side arms that answers a question the design left genuinely open. The meeple loop caps you at ONE meeple of each colour: a duplicate is returned to the box whether it came off your own Notice Board or off an island tile. That cap is doing two jobs at once and the shipped arm cannot tell them apart. It is the anti-pile rule, holding the supply flat so a leader cannot bank six visits; and it is a FORCING rule, because a colour you already hold is a colour you must spend before another can be gained, which is what keeps meeples circulating rather than sitting. This arm doubles it to two per colour and asks which job was load-bearing. THE PREDICTION IF THE CAP IS ANTI-PILE. Median supply in the last third rises, meeples boxed per game falls hard, and the visit rate barely moves, because a seat that already visits every turn cannot visit more; the cap was then costing components and teach for nothing and 2 is the friendlier number. THE PREDICTION IF THE CAP IS FORCING. Boxing falls and the visit rate falls WITH it, because meeples stop being use-them-or-lose-them and start being hoarded, which is precisely the failure v31's uncapped supply produced (45.8% of meeples ever spent, 7.00 dying unspent per game). READ IN THIS ORDER: (1) median supply held in the last third, against the shipped arm; (2) meeples boxed per game by source, island against collect; (3) the hook, rival visits per player per turn, which is the number that decides it; (4) the blocked-want rate, because a deeper supply is also a second answer to a blocked colour and may make the island alternative unnecessary; (5) the wild share of spends, which should fall if a second copy is easier to reach than a pair. A RESULT THAT MOVES NOTHING IS ITSELF THE FINDING: it would mean the supply is emptied every turn regardless and the cap is inert, in which case it should be deleted for teach cost alone. ⚠️ STATUS, 04/09/2026: the meeple loop is now the shipped default, so the visitCurrency line in this overlay's `set` is redundant and is left in place only because it documents what the arm is a variant OF. What this overlay still changes is meepleCapPerColour, and it is a LIVE VARIANT rather than a historical one: the cap stayed at 1 by Dean's ruling of 04/09/2026, taken AFTER this arm measured better than the shipped rule on both of its headline numbers (hook 0.40 against 0.37, and 7.67 meeples boxed a game against 13.41). That was a deliberate teach-simplicity decision - 'you may never hold two of a colour' is one sentence and a visible rule - and this overlay is what it cost, kept runnable so the price stays measurable.
